display.title: The Days of Sefirah: Respect for Others and the Precious Gift of Time
display.summary_short: Why there is no music during Sefirah, what Rabbi Akiva's students teach us about respect, and why every day we count is precious, with the story of a girl and her lost dime.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show during the days of Sefirah. Uncle Yossi explains why the program has no music in these weeks: they recall the sad time when thousands of Rabbi Akiva's students died in a plague because they did not show respect to one another. So Sefirah is a time to practice honor for parents, teachers and friends, to look at others with a good eye, avoid quarrels and make peace, as the Mishnah says, love peace and pursue it. Ahavas Yisroel and unity, led by the soldiers of Tzivos Hashem, are the answer to our cry of 'Ad Mosai'. He then explains that counting the Omer teaches that every day counts and each day should be better than the last. Time cannot be bought or brought back, as little Miriam learns when she keeps crying over a lost dime instead of caring for the ones her mother gives her. We should treasure and fill every day with Torah and mitzvos, and Hashem will lengthen our days.
display.lesson: Show respect to everyone, and treasure every day: time is Hashem's gift and lost time never returns.
